questions.q: What three parts make up one condition in the condition builder?
options: A field, an operator, and a value
A table, a column, and a row
A username, a role, and a permission
A form, a section, and a field
questions.explain: Each condition row is field / operator / value — for example Priority / is / 1 - Critical.

questions.q: What's the difference between combining two conditions with AND versus OR?
options: AND narrows the list to records matching both conditions; OR widens it to records matching either
AND and OR behave identically in the condition builder
OR always returns zero records
AND deletes records that match, OR keeps them
questions.explain: AND requires every stacked condition to match; OR matches if any one of them does, which widens the result set.

questions.q: What happens when you click a single breadcrumb pill above a filtered list?
options: It reopens the condition builder scoped to just that one condition, so you can edit it without touching the others
It permanently deletes that condition with no way to undo it
It closes the list entirely
It saves the whole filter as a new table
questions.explain: Breadcrumbs are clickable precisely so one condition can be edited in isolation, not just viewed.

questions.q: What is a saved Personal or shared list view, in relation to filters?
options: A filter you expect to reuse, saved so it doesn't need to be rebuilt from scratch every time
A completely separate copy of the table's data
A feature unrelated to the condition builder
A setting that only an admin can ever create
questions.explain: Saving a filter as a view is exactly how reusable, team-specific views like a "Service Desk view" come to exist.

questions.q: What does the encoded query `active=true^priority=1` represent?
options: A filter for active records AND priority 1, where ^ means AND
A filter for active records OR priority 1 records
A command that deletes all inactive, non-priority-1 records
A UI Policy script, not a filter
questions.explain: The caret (^) in an encoded query represents AND; ^OR would represent OR between conditions.
